test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 03 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: As per Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025, the percentage of population using an improved drinking water source in rural areas increased from 94.57% in 2015-16 to what percentage in 2024-25, indicating significant progress toward universal safe water access in rural India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.9962**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** aim to ensure universal access to safe drinking water by **2030**, as part of Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation).
 
• According to the **National Indicator Framework (NIF) Progress Report 2025**, the percentage of the population in rural areas using improved drinking water sources increased from **94.57%** in **2015-16** to **99.62%** in **2024-25**.
 
• Improved drinking water sources include **piped water supply, borewells, protected springs, and rainwater collection systems**, ensuring safe and reliable access.
 
• This progress highlights India's commitment to achieving the SDGs by addressing rural water challenges through programs such as the **Jal Jeevan Mission**.
 
• The increase from **94.57%** to **99.62%** represents a significant improvement, nearing universal access to safe drinking water in rural India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6):**

 
 
• It aims to ensure the availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all by **2030**.
 
• Key targets include achieving universal and equitable access to safe and affordable drinking water, improving water quality, and ensuring integrated water resource management.
 
 
 
• **Jal Jeevan Mission:**
 
 
• Launched in **2019**, this government initiative aims to provide functional household tap connections (FHTC) to every rural household by **2024**.
 
• It focuses on ensuring safe and adequate drinking water through individual household tap connections and strengthening water resource management.
 
 
 
• **National Indicator Framework (NIF):**
 
 
• The NIF is a framework developed by the Indian government to monitor progress on the SDGs at the national and sub-national levels.
 
• It consists of a set of indicators aligned with the SDGs to track India's performance and highlight areas needing improvement.
 
 
 
• **Improved Drinking Water Sources:**
 
 
• These include piped water on premises, public taps, tube wells, boreholes, protected dug wells, protected springs, and rainwater collection systems.
 
• Such sources are less likely to be contaminated and are considered reliable for safe drinking water.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Progress in Rural Water Access:**

 
 
• The increase from **94.57%** to **99.62%** indicates significant progress under government initiatives like **Jal Jeevan Mission** and **Swachh Bharat Mission**.
 
• It reflects improved infrastructure, better management, and community participation in water resource management.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Achieving Universal Access:**
 
 
• Despite progress, challenges remain in terms of water quality, contamination, and equitable access in remote or underdeveloped areas.
 
• Ongoing efforts are required to address these challenges and ensure sustainable water resource management.
